Gaming is evolving from what it once was.

We used to play using VGA graphics and worse earlier on, now we don't, although that is still an option. Retro graphics are still quite popular and being used, same as older game mechanics can still be used if the developer wants to.

The idea that gaming has been dumbed down over the years is complete bullshit.

Games used to be hard because we lacked a means to save progress forcing one to play it all in one sitting, and then later on adopted level checkpoint codes you could enter to skip ahead. Games used to be hard because they were designed to make you die over and over again to feed the machines quarters, and then moved away from the system of lives and continues as it made no sense to have outside an arcade machine. Games used to be hard because when you played those hard ones, you were a small child and have since developed decades of experience to play new ones.

For the actual topical part of your reply... You say it's for the challenge, but I specifically addressed that. Checkpoints are very often spaced so far apart that you are forced to repeat mundane tasks which just end up frustrating the player. The challenge is not if you can walk across a hall, but rather the boss battle where you died initially. Having to walk through the hall time and time again to get back to the battle and thus the fun part will only serve to make the player frustrated which is the exact oppose of the purpose of gaming.

As fro strolling through and cheats, I guess you have not played many modern games. If I wanted to just fuck around and destroy my progress on a lark, I could with anytime saves and pick back up where I had left off.
